newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany, France back U.N. reform plans.
newsitem.headline: Germany, France back U.N. reform plans.

text.p: Germany and France on Thursday applauded the sweeping reforms plans for the United Nations bureaucracy announced by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and promised to support the measures fully.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Annan was sending a positive signal and it was now up to the 185 U.N. member nations to throw their support behind the proposals.

"We cannot allow the impetus that the Secretary-General has given to the reform with his report to be talked to death," Kinkel said in a statement. "We need a slimmed down, efficient U.N. today more than ever."

In Paris, French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a daily briefing that France would support Annan in his attempt to flesh out proposals "which for the main part were suggested by the European Union."
"We will be vigilant to ensure that the fruits of the reform benefit countries of the third world first of all, as the Secretary-General has promised," Rummelhardt said.
Annan, presenting his package of proposals to streamline the U.N. bureaucracy, urged governments to cut back programmes they were responsible for instituting.
"The reforms of such a huge organisation as the U.N. obviously cannot take place overnight," Kinkel said.

"There has been talk about the need for reform for years. Secretary-General Annan has done his share of the work. Now the 185 member states have to use the 52nd General Assembly in September to back the reform measures."
